title: Fan Selection Workflow
description: Clickable twelve-step Mermaid flowchart of the fan selection workflow, from application requirements to the specification, with an eight-card sorting check in which learners assign job information to the step that uses it and get the reason after each card.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: application engineers, sales staff, representatives, distributors and specifying engineers
learningObjectives: The learner will classify eight pieces of application information by the selection step that uses them, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.

accessibility.notes: Flowchart nodes are focusable buttons (Tab, then Enter or Space reads a step); Enter submits the chosen step and goes to the next card; verdicts and step explanations announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour on nodes, feedback and progress chips; the phase key gives step ranges as well as colours.

controls.label: Workflow step
controls.purpose: Choose the step that uses the card's information

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Assign the card to the chosen step; one attempt, then the card locks (Enter)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Sort the same eight cards again in the same order, score cleared

rules: Each card has exactly one correct step.
A card can be assigned once; it locks after submission.
Score is the count of correct first assignments out of 8; mastery is a score of 7 or more.
Clicking flowchart steps is exploration and is never scored.
limitations: The job values on the cards are one illustrative worked example.

sources: Step order and content from Chapter 27's sections. The 1,450, 1,180 and 1,780 RPM values, the 500°F and 70°F temperatures, the 95 dB limit and the 10 ft by 8 ft pad are the chapter's illustrative worked example.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a clickable workflow, then classify job information into workflow steps with immediate explanatory feedback
keyQuestions: Which selection step consumes this piece of job information?
When a candidate fails the sound or dimension check, which step does the selection loop back to?
Why is the motor sized for the coldest start rather than the hot design temperature?
commonMisconceptions: Selection is finished once a size is read from the performance table.
The motor is sized from the operating brake horsepower at the hot design temperature.
Dimensions are checked only after the order is placed.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'Cards correct: n of 8'; mastery is 7 of 8 on the first attempt.
Follow-up: given a requirement change, name the step the selection loops back to.
